featured_reviews.name: jay sanghavi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Title: Disappointed with Lack of Discounts for Regular Blood Donations

Review:

I have been an active blood donor for several years, and I have participated in numerous blood donation camps organized by various organizations. While I appreciate the efforts made by ANVISHKA (GHATKOPAR WEST MUMBAI ) in collecting and distributing blood, I am deeply disappointed by the lack of recognition and benefits given to regular donors like myself.

Throughout the years, I have diligently donated my blood, always carrying my proof cards as evidence of my contributions. However, despite my consistent efforts, I have never received any discounts on blood when I required it during my own medical emergencies. I find this disheartening, as it seems that ANVISHKA does not value the loyalty and dedication of the blood donors

It is not unreasonable to expect some form of acknowledgment or incentive for those of us who selflessly give our blood to help others. Other blood banks and organizations often provide discounts or priority access to regular donors, recognizing their commitment and encouraging them to continue their vital contributions.

I sincerely hope that ANVISHKA takes this feedback into consideration and reevaluates their policies regarding discounts for regular blood donors. Acknowledging and rewarding the generosity of individuals who consistently support their cause would not only foster a stronger bond with the donor community but also motivate others to become regular blood donors.

I still believe in the importance of blood donation and will continue to contribute to the cause, but I hope ANVISHKA reconsiders their stance on recognizing the dedication of their regular donors.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently donated blood at this blood bank and was informed that my blood had tested positive for hepatitis C antibodies using the ELISA Generation 4 method. Naturally, this news was extremely concerning, so I took it upon myself to get retested at a private lab. The private lab conducted two tests—one using the rapid method and the other using the ELFA method. Both of these tests came back negative for hepatitis C antibodies. To be absolutely sure, I also did an HCV RNA PCR test, which is the most reliable test for detecting an active hepatitis C infection. Thankfully, the result was "NOT DETECTED," meaning there was no active virus in my blood.

This whole experience has caused me unnecessary stress and confusion. I fully understand that antibody tests can sometimes give false positives, but I believe the blood bank should be more cautious and thorough before alarming donors with such serious results. Furthermore, after receiving the initial notification, I reached out to the blood bank multiple times seeking guidance on what to do next, but they have stopped responding to my queries. They haven’t provided any further support, leaving me in the dark about whether I can donate blood in the future or what steps I should take.

This lack of communication and support from the blood bank is extremely disappointing, especially when dealing with such sensitive health concerns. I advise others to be cautious and double-check their results if they receive any alarming notifications from this blood bank. I hope the blood bank improves their processes, both in terms of accuracy and in providing proper guidance to donors.

featured_reviews.name: shailesh mulaye
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst Hospital Experience Ever

I am writing this review to warn others about my extremely bad experience at Adi Arogyam Hospital. This hospital is highly disappointing in almost every aspect and completely fails to meet basic medical and ethical standards.

Firstly, the reception and front-desk staff are extremely careless. There is no proper guidance regarding procedures, or waiting time. Patients are left confused and stressed, especially elderly people and those in pain. Despite repeated requests, no one was willing to provide clear information.

The waiting time is unreasonably long, even for simple consultations. Patients are made to sit for hours without any explanation or updates. This shows a complete lack of respect for people’s time and suffering.

When the time of discharge patient they give the settlement amount in check that is more than 10000/- there is the no facilities to give the settlement amount in cash and also the refund amount they take 4 month and more

Account department also not cooperating for the refund process when the patient visit to hospital several time for the refund

The billing and administrative process is completely non-transparent. Charges were not explained properly, and unexpected amounts were added to the bill without justification. When clarification was requested, the staff behaved arrogantly and avoided giving proper answers. This creates a strong feeling of cheating and exploitation of patients.

Overall, this hospital shows zero compassion, zero professionalism, and zero accountability. Patient care seems to be the last priority here. I regret choosing Adi Arogyam Hospital and would strongly advise others to avoid this hospital if they value their health, money, and peace of mind.

This review is based on my personal experience, and I hope the hospital management takes serious action instead of ignoring patient feedback.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Mr Shailesh,

We respect your feedback, but we would like to clarify that the delay in refund was not due to hospital negligence. The majority of your refund was processed the very next day after discharge. Only a small remaining amount was pending due to insurance processing timelines, which were completely beyond the hospital’s control. Our team continuously followed up and supported the process.
We regret any inconvenience caused and remain committed to fair, transparent and ethical patient care.

— Adi Arogyam Hospital Management

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Aparaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
My father was admitted this month under CGHS benefits for diabetic foot surgery. As very few hospitals in Mumbai are empanelled under Central Government Health Schemes, we were relieved to get admission here.

The OPD procedures went smoothly. We were later informed that the patient would need to be admitted for a short duration (around two days) for surgical treatment. Since a private room was unavailable at the time, we opted for a multi-sharing ward.

Overall, the surgical treatment and interactions with the doctors and specialists were excellent. Dr. Rajeev Singh and his team took great care of the patient and kept us informed about the surgery schedule in advance, ensuring the admission was not done unnecessarily early.

However, the experience with the nursing staff was disappointing. Routine procedures were frequently delayed, and when assistance was requested, the behaviour was often rude towards both patients and visitors. In contrast, the ward-boy staff were more cooperative, welcoming, and helpful.

The discharge process was particularly frustrating. It began around 10:30 AM, but the paperwork was not handled in a timely manner and took over six hours to complete. There was no clear communication, and responsibility for delays was repeatedly shifted between departments. Since both of my parents and many other patients in the ward are diabetic, such prolonged delays are especially challenging. This is not an overreaction, but a genuine concern.

Additionally, the behaviour at the cashier counter was unprofessional. The staff member was rude, provided no estimate of waiting time, did not manage the queue properly, and even threatened to call security when questioned politely.

I understand that healthcare jobs demand immense patience and resilience, but this also comes with a responsibility to maintain professionalism and empathy, especially towards patients who are already vulnerable.

I am unsure whether these issues stem from hospital management or understaffing, but there is clearly room for improvement and accountability.

Despite these concerns, I remain grateful for the medical care and treatment provided by the doctors and the hospital overall.

featured_reviews.name: Suraaj Dubey
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the hospital for blood donation with a genuine intention to help others. During the screening, I was told that my hemoglobin level was low. However, after further tests, everything came out normal and there was no health issue found.

I feel the staff handling the blood donation process need better training and proper knowledge. Hiring inexperienced staff without enough medical understanding can create unnecessary fear and confusion for donors. Because of this, people who come forward for a good cause may feel discouraged from donating blood again.

I hope the hospital management improves staff training and ensures accurate guidance is given to donors in the future.

featured_reviews.name: रुबाब FASHION HUB'S
featured_reviews.review_text:
The staff at this blood bank are very useless and have very low level of ideology. I was sent by the doctor at Satabdi Hospital to help an elderly man and ordered emergency blood. They delayed the payment for a long time. When I was making the payment, I was given a cash payment. There is no change for 500 rs in such a big blood bank. They made me check it from the shop next door. The staff is very terrible in such an emergency.

Very bad service

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Limaye
featured_reviews.review_text: They are a shame on humanity. They take a non refundable deposit of ₹450 , do not give receipt, no terms clearly explained. My dad was being operated upon in SUVARNA Hospital Borivali west and we had requested for reservation of blood on 19.03.2026. Fortunately we did not need blood on 20.03 and 21.03 but we were in need of blood unit for 22.03.2026.When we called them, they said it is over 24 hours so you will have to pay deposit again . Basically a con game to get ₹450 as advance and refuse to accept it later ( within 48 hours). This is absolute inhuman behaviour from the blood bank. They will have a curse of a million people if they continue to operate with such foolish money mindset with no respect to customer inconvenience and do not bother to give any receipts or  explain these terms before making reservation. They should be closed down on unethical business practices.

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek kamath
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best blood bank to donate your blood. The process was smooth and calm. They gave me a card which has a 1 year validity so if a peron needs blood within that period they will get 400rs discount.

featured_reviews.name: Sonia Premchandani
featured_reviews.review_text: Needed blood for my ailing relative.was guided to navjivan blood bank.best Centre.. to avail blood .thanks navjivan for the prompt service and support given..as I am new to this place.

featured_reviews.name: nayana pawar
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst experience.Irresponsible staff they don’t care about patients life my patient admitted in the Karuna hospital I had call twiced to confirm for irradiated SDP platelets there staff said yes u will get and after payment done they are saying they don’t have any idea the radiation department is closed and gave me so many reasons and not gave me refund.

featured_reviews.name: Ketan Thakkar
featured_reviews.review_text: As a blood bank, you supplied four phone numbers, but none of them are working; why write 24 hours a day, seven days a week when all of them are disconnected? I attempted to contact about donating blood and verifying operating times. Assume someone needs blood. How will they connect in an emergency? If anyone knows the owner or trustee, please notify them. Also, please advise a reputable blood bank in Kandivali / Borivali, as I started donating blood every six months.
